# Exploring viral diversity through data {.no-anchor}

**BioVirLab** brings together researchers dedicated to the discovery,
characterisation and evolutionary analysis of viruses, combining
high-throughput sequencing, bioinformatics and experimental validation. Our work
ranges from identifying novel viruses in environmental and biological samples to
studying the mechanisms of virus–host interaction.

# The laboratory

We work at the interface between computational biology and virology, using
metagenomic and metatranscriptomic data to reconstruct viral genomes, infer
phylogenetic relationships and describe the diversity of viruses associated with
invertebrates, plants, vertebrates and natural environments.

Beyond basic research, the laboratory develops open computational workflows and
tools for the scientific community, and maintains continuous training activities
for undergraduate and graduate students.

::: {.card-grid}
::: {.info-card}
### Virus discovery

Identification and characterisation of novel viruses from large-scale
sequencing data, with manual curation and experimental validation.
:::

::: {.info-card}
### Genomics and evolution

Genome reconstruction, functional annotation and phylogenetic analyses to
understand the origin and diversification of viral lineages.
:::

::: {.info-card}
### Open tools

Development of reproducible pipelines and software for virome analysis, released
in public repositories.
:::

::: {.info-card}
### Scientific training

Supervision of undergraduate, MSc and PhD students, with an emphasis on critical
thinking and open science.
:::
:::

# Where we are

<!-- AJUSTAR: confirmar endereco, departamento e contato institucional -->

BioVirLab is based at the **State University of Santa Cruz (UESC)** and at the
**Federal University of Southern Bahia (UFSB)**, in the cities of Ilhéus and
Itabuna — Bahia, Brazil.
